The owner's light interactivity for a scene, kept beside it as the <id>.interact.json sidecar: hotspots (a pin on a surface with a card — title, text, image, price tag, a call-to-action such as "Book a visit" or a WhatsApp link, an optional "Fly there" camera), interactive objects (a picked door, piece of furniture or lamp with an action: door open/close by hinge or slide, visibility, material finish switch, light switch, clip glTF animation) with their triggers (click, near with a radius, a guided-tour tour stop) and the scene toggles (daynight, empty — hides the furniture group, measure). The viewer authors it with ?interact=edit (signed in); every viewer of the scene gets it. The schema and its limits (64 hotspots, 64 objects, 64 KB) live in web/playground/interact-core.js, which both the server and the viewer run: URLs must be https:/http:, tel:, mailto:, whatsapp: or a same-site path, images https: or same-site. GET mirrors the scene's visibility (private: owner or share token) and answers 204 when nothing is saved; PUT is owner-only and returns the stored, sanitized document; {"clear": true} removes it. Same delete rules as the other sidecars. Errors: 400 invalid JSON · 401 · 404 not the owner's scene · 413 over 64 KB. Hotspot opens, call-to-action clicks and object use reach the owner's analytics as act rows (hotspot, cta, object; telemetry).

Ground heightfield (2.7, exterior kit)#

PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/ground#

Code
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/ground -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: image/png" --data-binary @terrain.png
# {"scene":"SCENE","path":"ingest/SCENE.ground.png","url":"https://HOST/ingest/SCENE.ground.png","width":1024,"height":1024,"bytes":412233}

Owner-only. The body is a PNG (≤ 4096 × 4096, ≤ 8 MB; the red channel is the height, 0–255 → 0–amplitude metres) stored as the scene's <id>.ground.png sidecar — the same visibility, version and delete rules as the poster (a private scene gates it; deleting the scene removes it). The exterior kit displaces its ground with it when ground.kind is heightfield and ground.heightfield points at the path (the Exterior panel's Upload does both); the walker stands on the displaced ground. Re-uploading replaces the file. Errors: 400 not a PNG / over 4096² · 401 · 404 not the owner's scene · 413 over 8 MB.

Configurator: a scene's configuration schema (2.7)#

2.5 switched one KHR_materials_variants name from ?variant=. The configuration schema is the owner's layer on top: option groups ("Fabric", "Legs", "Size"), each option mapping to a material variant and/or explicit material aliases (multi-material groups) and/or a visibility set, with an optional SKU and a display-only price. The viewer shows it as a panel, the embed SDK as setConfiguration() / getConfiguration() / the configuration event, and the whole pick rides the link as ?cfg=fabric:oak,legs:black (only non-default picks). Guide: docs/guides/build-a-configurator.md.

Code
{
  "title": "Configure",
  "currency": "USD",
  "base": 890,
  "groups": [
    { "id": "fabric", "name": "Fabric", "default": "oak",
      "options": [
        { "id": "oak",    "name": "Oak",    "variant": "Oak" },
        { "id": "walnut", "name": "Walnut", "variant": "Walnut", "price": 120, "sku": "SOFA-WAL" } ] },
    { "id": "legs", "name": "Legs",
      "options": [
        { "id": "steel", "name": "Steel", "materials": { "4": 7 }, "swatch": "#8a8f98" },
        { "id": "none",  "name": "No legs", "hide": [4], "price": -40 } ] }
  ]
}

Rules (web/playground/config.js normalizeConfig, the same code the viewer renders with): ≤ 16 groups × 32 options; ids [a-z0-9_-]{1,32} (slugged from the name when omitted); variant must name one of the scene's variants; materials is {dst: src} glTF material indices (dst draws as src); hide lists material indices the option blacks out (the engine has no per-material hide lane yet — the IFC hidden mask replaces this); price is a number ≥ 0 rounded to cents, sku ≤ 48 chars, swatch #rrggbb. Later groups win a material conflict. Nothing here bills: the price total is a label.

GET /v1/scenes/<id>/config#

Public, mirroring the scene's visibility (a private scene needs the owner's auth or ?share=; strangers get the same 404 as a missing scene) → { "scene", "config", "updated" }, Cache-Control: no-store. 204 No Content when the scene has no schema — the viewer probes this on every streamed-scene open.

PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/config#

Code
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @schema.json
# {"scene":"SCENE","config":{"version":1,"groups":[…]},"warnings":["option \"x\": unknown variant \"Teak\""]}

Owner-only (60/hour/IP). Body = the schema (or {"config": <schema>}); {"groups": []} / {"config": null} clears it. The response carries the canonical form (ids filled, defaults set) and warnings for anything dropped. Fires the config.changed webhook. Errors: 400 nothing usable (errors lists why) · 401 · 404 not the owner's scene · 413 over 64 KB.

Media surfaces + spatial audio (2.7)#

An owner puts a video on a surface and ambient sounds in the room (?author=1 → Media, docs/guides/video-and-audio.md). The table lives in the scene's staging manifest (<id>.stage.json: media, audio) and follows the scene through versions; because that file is served immutable, the viewer reads it through the no-store route below.

GET /v1/scenes/<id>/media#

Public, mirroring the scene's visibility (a private scene needs the owner's auth or a share token; strangers get a missing scene's 404) → { "scene", "media": [{ "material", "url", "loop", "emissive", "audio" }], "audio": [{ "pos", "url", "radius", "loop", "gain" }] }, Cache-Control: no-store. 204 No Content when the scene has neither.

PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/media#

Code
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/media -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"media":[{"material":3,"url":"/ingest/SCENE.media/1.mp4","emissive":1.5,"audio":true}],
       "audio":[{"pos":[2,1.2,-1],"url":"/ingest/SCENE.media/2.mp3","radius":6,"gain":0.8}]}'
# {"scene":"SCENE","media":[...],"audio":[...]}   (normalized)

Owner-only; replaces the whole table (≤ 32 KB). media: at most 4 surfaces (the renderer's media layers), each a distinct glTF material index with a same-origin video url (/ingest/<id>.media/<n>.mp4 from the upload route, or any path on this host — cross-origin URLs are refused: the frame is read back on the GPU and must not be tainted), loop (default true), emissive glow 0–8 (default 1) and audio (default false: play the video's own sound from the surface). audio: at most 16 ambient emitters, pos [x, y, z], same-origin url, radius 0.5–200 m (linear rolloff to silence), loop, gain 0–2. Errors: 400 validation (the message names the field) · 401 · 404 not the owner's scene · 409 the scene has no staging manifest (a classic GLB scene; media surfaces need a streamed scene).

POST /v1/scenes/<id>/media/upload#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/media/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" --data-binary @tv-loop.mp4
# {"path":"ingest/SCENE.media/1.mp4","url":"https://HOST/ingest/SCENE.media/1.mp4","bytes":4188212,"kind":"video","ext":"mp4"}
  • Body: one raw media file, container-sniffed (the header's type is ignored): mp4 (ISO BMFF; M4A brands count as audio) or webm (EBML; a video track makes it video) for video, ≤ 200 MB; mp3, m4a, ogg, wav or audio-only webm for audio, ≤ 20 MB. The cap is chosen from the sniff, so an over-cap body is refused as soon as it crosses its line.
  • Stored as ingest/<id>.media/<n>.<ext> (n counts up per scene), served with the scene's visibility (a private scene's clip needs the owner's auth or ?share=), Range-capable (so <video> seeks), deleted with the scene. Put the returned path (root-relative) in a surface's or emitter's url.
  • Errors: 400 not a media file we serve · 401 / 404 as PUT · 413 over the cap for its kind · 500.

Web games#

Host an HTML5 game from a .zip and play it on its own origin, play.ctruh.io (Host a web game). Owner routes need an account token.

RouteDoes
POST /v1/gamesraw .zip body, X-Verse-Name: <file name>, optional X-Verse-Title; answers the game record (id, player and embed URLs, dropped-file count)
POST /v1/ingest with X-Verse-Kind: gamethe same, through the upload road (also chosen when a zip has an index.html and scripts)
POST /v1/games/<id>/replacea new build, same link
PATCH /v1/games/<id>{title, visibility, isolation, orientation}
PUT /v1/games/<id>/coverPNG, JPG or WebP up to 3 MB; GET …/cover (a Ctruh card when none)
POST /v1/games/<id>/sharea private share code
DELETE /v1/games/<id>remove the game
GET /v1/account/gamesthe owner's library

Limits come from the plan: zip size 100 MB Free, 500 MB Starter, 1 GB Pro, 2 GB Scale; three games on Free. Zips are refused with a plain reason for more than 4,000 files, more than five times the plan size once unpacked, symlinks, absolute or .. paths, or a password.

Embeds#

Guide: Embed anywhere. Plug-ins: integrations/embeds/ (WordPress, Shopify, Webflow). Product pages: 3D on product pages, integrations/commerce/ (WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, Salesforce Commerce Cloud).

oEmbed#

GET /oembed?url=<share link>&maxwidth=<px>&maxheight=<px>&format=json (public, CORS *, rate-limited 1200/h per IP)

Answers for share links on this server's host and on verse.ctruh.com (more: VERSE_OEMBED_HOSTS=a.example,b.example). A link is /, /app, /view or /embed with vpk=, glb=, model= or scene=; look options on the link (look, bg, env, variant, cfg, lights, view, sky, weather, fog, ground, select, experience, tour) and aspect=16:9|4:3|1:1|3:4|9:16|21:9, load=tap, analytics=0 carry into the embed.

Code
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "type": "rich",
  "provider_name": "Ctruh Verse",
  "provider_url": "https://verse.ctruh.com/",
  "title": "Palm villa",
  "html": "<div class=\"verse-embed\" style=\"position:relative;width:100%;max-width:640px;aspect-ratio:16/9;margin:0 auto\"><iframe src=\"https://verse.ctruh.com/embed?vpk=ingest/palm-villa-0a1b2c3d4e5f.vpk\" title=\"Palm villa — 3D view\" loading=\"lazy\" allow=\"fullscreen; xr-spatial-tracking; accelerometer; gyroscope; magnetometer; autoplay; clipboard-write\" allowfullscreen referrerpolicy=\"strict-origin-when-cross-origin\" style=\"…\"></iframe></div>",
  "width": 640,
  "height": 360,
  "cache_age": 3600,
  "thumbnail_url": "https://verse.ctruh.com/ingest/palm-villa-0a1b2c3d4e5f.poster.png",
  "thumbnail_width": 1200,
  "thumbnail_height": 630
}
  • Size. width = maxwidth (default 640, at most 1920); height from the aspect ratio (16:9; Fidelity products 1:1; or the link's aspect), shrunk to maxheight. The html is responsive whatever the numbers: it fills its container up to width.
  • Title. The scene's name from its id (palm-villa-<12 hex> → "Palm villa").
  • Thumbnail. The owner's attached poster, else the auto poster (<id>.poster.png), with its real pixel size. Omitted when the scene has none.
  • Private scenes. The link must carry a valid share token (&share=<token>), or the request the owner's auth. The html and thumbnail_url then carry the token, and the answer is Cache-Control: private, no-store with cache_age: 0. Without access the answer is exactly the unknown-scene answer: 404 {"error":"not found"}, same headers.
  • Errors. 400 no url; 404 not a Verse scene link, a foreign host, an unknown scene or a private one without access; 501 format other than json; 429 rate limit.

Share-page tags#

A share page that names a scene (/?vpk=…, /view?glb=…, /app?…) carries, right after its <title>: <link rel="alternate" type="application/json+oembed"> (oEmbed discovery), Open Graph (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image = the poster or the site image, with og:image:width/height) and a Twitter summary_large_image card. A private scene's page gets them only with a valid token (plus robots: noindex); without one the page is the plain app page, the same as for an unknown scene.

GET /embed#

The lazy embed card that the oEmbed html, the plug-ins and Studio's embed code frame. The same query as embed.html (vpk / glb / model / scene, look options, share, analytics=0) plus:

ParameterEffect
load=tapLoad the 3D on tap only (also the default when the browser asks to save data)
guard=0No scroll guard: the scene takes every gesture from the start (default: vertical swipes and the wheel scroll the host page until the visitor taps / clicks the scene)
fs=0No fullscreen button (default: top-right; links out to /view where the frame cannot go fullscreen, as on iPhone)
ar=0No "View in AR" control (default: shown where the device can place the scene — WebXR, or Quick Look on iOS)

It is one small HTML page: the scene's poster and title inlined, no engine. When it is 25 % visible (IntersectionObserver), or on tap, it replaces itself with embed.html (the engine), keeping the poster behind the canvas until the first frame. Headers: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (on /embed.html too), so pages that are themselves cross-origin isolated can frame it; no X-Frame-Options. A private scene without a token gets the generic card (no title, no poster), identical to an unknown scene's.

Review comments#

Pinned comments in 3D space on a shared scene — the client-review workflow. Access mirrors the scene: public and unlisted scenes are open to anyone with the link; a private scene's comments need the owner's auth or a share token (?share= / X-Verse-Share). Strangers see 404.

Storage is a per-scene append-only JSONL under ingest/.reviews/ (never served, deleted with the scene).

POST /v1/review/<sceneId>#

No account required; 60/hour/IP.

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"pos":[1.2,0.9,-0.4],"text":"Can we see this wall in the oak finish?","author":"Priya"}'
# {"id":"c76ae3e41a","t":1790833830642}
  • Body: { pos: [x, y, z], text ≤ 500 chars (required), author? ≤ 40 }. - Errors: 400 invalid shape · 404 no such scene, or private without access · 413 text over 500 chars or the scene already at 200 comments · 429.

GET /v1/review/<sceneId>#

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84
# {"scene":"docs-demo-718035483f84","comments":[{"id":"c76ae3e41a","t":1790833830642,
#   "pos":[1.2,0.9,-0.4],"text":"Can we see this wall in the oak finish?","author":"Priya","resolved":false}]}

Oldest first; resolved comments included. 404 for a private scene without access.

POST /v1/review/<sceneId>/<id>/resolve · DELETE /v1/review/<sceneId>/<id>#

Owner-of-scene moderation (Bearer token or cookie).

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84/c76ae3e41a/resolve -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# {"id":"c76ae3e41a","resolved":true}
curl -sS -X DELETE https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84/c76ae3e41a -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# {"deleted":"c76ae3e41a"}
  • Errors: 401 no account auth · 404 not the owner, or no such comment · 429 (shares the scene-management bucket).

GET /v1/account/scenes carries reviews: { open, total } per scene. Guide: Collect client review comments.

Publishing: experiences, tours, posters#

No API key required; 30/hour/IP; account auth stamps an owner. All three return { "path", "url" } with a server-chosen random id.

POST /v1/experience#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/experience -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Docs showroom","scene":"ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk",
       "hotspots":[{"id":"front","label":"Front","position":[0,1.2,3],"look":[0,0.5,0]}]}'
# {"path":"ingest/exp-38fd878a72.verse.json","url":"https://HOST/?experience=ingest/exp-38fd878a72.verse.json"}
  • Body: a .verse.json manifest (Experience manifests), max 128 KB; scene (non-empty string) is required, everything else is validated by the runtime parser on load.
  • Errors: 400 not JSON or scene missing · 500 could not store.
  • With account auth the owner stamp also records the manifest's scene and name, which is what GET /v1/scenes/<id>/experiences lists.

GET /v1/experience/<id> · PUT /v1/experience/<id> (2.7)#

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/experience/exp-38fd878a72
# {"id":"exp-38fd878a72","path":"ingest/exp-38fd878a72.verse.json","experience":{...}}
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/experience/exp-38fd878a72 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @manifest.json
# {"id":"exp-38fd878a72","path":"ingest/exp-38fd878a72.verse.json","url":"https://HOST/?experience=/v1/experience/exp-38fd878a72"}
  • GET is public (mirrors the scene's visibility) and no-store: the static ingest/exp-<id>.verse.json copy is served immutable for a year, so anything that may have been edited — the Author bar, Studio, embeds — reads through here. ?experience=/v1/experience/<id> is the share-link spelling the Author bar hands out.
  • PUT is owner-only (401 no auth, 404 not yours), same body rules as POST (≤ 128 KB, scene required), rewrites the manifest in place and refreshes the scene/name stamp.

POST /v1/experience/<id>/media (2.7)#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/experience/exp-38fd878a72/media -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: audio/mpeg" --data-binary @kitchen.mp3
# {"path":"ingest/exp-38fd878a72-media-9a1b2c3d.mp3","url":"https://HOST/ingest/exp-38fd878a72-media-9a1b2c3d.mp3","bytes":381204}
  • Body: a raw narration clip, max 2 MB, container-sniffed — mp3 (ID3 / frame sync), m4a (ftyp), ogg, wav (RIFF/WAVE) or webm (EBML); the stored extension follows the sniff, never the header. Put the returned path (root-relative) in a tour step's audio.
  • Errors: 400 not an audio clip · 401 / 404 as PUT · 413 over 2 MB · 500. Clips are bounded as a set (VERSE_MAX_MEDIA, default 2000 kept) like posters and tours.

POST /v1/tour#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/tour -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"docs tour","scene":"ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk",
       "samples":[[0,0,1.6,3,0,0,-1],[4,3,1.6,0,-1,0,0]]}'
# {"path":"ingest/tour-488fd5fe4b.tour.json","url":"https://HOST/?tour=ingest/tour-488fd5fe4b.tour.json"}
  • Body: { name?, scene, samples }, max 512 KB; samples is 2–6000 rows of [t, x, y, z, fx, fy, fz] (finite numbers); name truncated to 120 chars. The viewer lerps between rows and loops.
  • Errors: 400 invalid shape (the body says what) · 500.

POST /v1/poster#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/poster -H "Content-Type: image/png" --data-binary @poster.png
# {"path":"ingest/poster-748cf2228b.png","url":"https://HOST/ingest/poster-748cf2228b.png"}
  • Body: raw PNG, max 4 MB, magic-checked. With account auth, X-Verse-Scene: <owned scene id> attaches it as that scene's dashboard thumbnail; ?scene=<id> (used by the viewer's automatic first-visit capture) stores it idempotently as ingest/<id>.poster.png.
  • Errors: 400 not a PNG · 500.

Presence rooms#

Live-tour presence: a room is a named set of viewers who see each other's camera pose. HTTP only (SSE out, tiny POSTs in); poses are memory-only, 10 s TTL — nothing is recorded and a restart empties every room. <room> is 1–64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; treat room ids as capability URLs.

GET /v1/room/<room>/events#

text/event-stream, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The roster arrives on connect and then on change, coalesced to ≤ ~10 frames/s:

Code
data: {"peers":[{"id":"docs-viewer-1","name":"Docs","color":"#78aaff","pose":[0,1.6,3,0,0,-1],"flags":{}}]}

2.7 (voice + presenter): open the stream as ?id=<your peer id> and it is tagged — signals addressed to that id arrive on it as named events. The first frame on a tagged or untagged stream is the config:

Code
event: config
data: {"ice":[{"urls":["stun:stun.l.google.com:19302","stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302"]}],"mesh":6}

event: signal
data: {"from":"docs-viewer-2","to":"docs-viewer-1","kind":"offer","data":{"type":"offer","sdp":"..."},"t":1760000000000}

ice is the STUN list from VERSE_STUN (comma-separated stun: URLs; none → []); mesh is the voice mesh cap (6 talkers per room). Each peer's flags object carries whichever of presenter, hand, muted, voice, ptt, host (the live tour's host) are set and the presenter's laser point [x, y, z]. The stream carries a comment line (: hb <ms>) every 5 s as a heartbeat: a client that sees 15 s of silence should reopen it. Older clients that ignore named events keep working unchanged.

POST /v1/room/<room>/pose#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/room/docs-room/pose -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"docs-viewer-1","name":"Docs","color":"#78aaff","pose":[0,1.6,3,0,0,-1]}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
  • Body ≤ 2 KB: id 4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-] (client-invented), name ≤ 24, color #rrggbb, pose up to 6 numbers, optional flags {presenter?, hand?, muted?, voice?, ptt?, host?, laser?: [x, y, z]} (2.7; booleans are kept only when true, anything else is dropped). Post at ~8 Hz; peers expire after 10 s of silence.
  • Errors: 400 bad id or room full (32 peers).

POST /v1/room/<room>/signal#

Relay for voice signalling and presenter events (2.7). The server forwards the body verbatim and at once to the SSE stream(s) opened with ?id=<to> — or, for to: "*", to every tagged stream in the room except the sender's — and keeps nothing. No audio ever passes through here: voice is WebRTC peer-to-peer and only the SDP / ICE text is relayed.

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/room/docs-room/signal -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"docs-viewer-2","to":"docs-viewer-1","kind":"offer","data":{"type":"offer","sdp":"..."}}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
# X-Verse-Delivered: 1
  • Body ≤ 16 KB: from and to peer ids (4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-]; to may be "*"), kind one of offer answer ice bye mute (voice), present action laser hand handover (presenter), chat, ping end (live tour, below); data any JSON.
  • Reply: 204 with X-Verse-Delivered: <n> — the number of streams the frame was written to (0 = that peer is not listening; nothing is queued).
  • Errors: 400 bad id / kind, 413 over 16 KB, 429 over 400 signals per second per room (ICE bursts are ~30 per peer), 429 too many rooms.
  • Presenter event schema (kind: "action", to: "*"), applied by followers through the same setters the UI uses: {name: "tour", detail: {playing}} · {name: "hotspot", detail: {id}} · {name: "variant", detail: {name}} · {name: "lights", detail: {query}} (a ?lights= string) · {name: "clip", detail: {encoded}} (a ?clip= string; the embed may send {planes: [[nx,ny,nz,d]…], cap} instead) · {name: "style", detail: {name}} (the restyle agent's ?style= look). present {on} announces / gives up the floor, handover {} (addressed) makes the recipient present, hand {} is a raised hand, mute {muted} mirrors the roster flag so a mute shows before the next pose post.
  • Privacy: the room id is the capability, exactly as for the roster. There is no TURN relay: two peers that both sit behind symmetric NAT never connect and the viewer says so ("no audio with …") rather than failing silently.

Tour together, live#

An agent's one tap mints a short invite link; a buyer opens it on any phone (WhatsApp / Instagram in-app browsers included) and lands in the agent's room as a guest who follows the host's camera. Three routes on top of the presence room, all memory only — an invite is {scene, room, created, expires}, no account, no name, no address; the room name is the capability and the code only shortens it. Guide: Tour together.

POST /v1/tour/invite#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/tour/invite -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scene":"ingest/5f2c…e1.vpk"}'
# {"code":"k7m2xq4","url":"https://HOST/t/k7m2xq4","room":"tour-m8w3q2vk7p","scene":"ingest/5f2c…e1.vpk",
#  "expiresAt":1760100000000,"landing":"/view?vpk=ingest%2F5f2c…e1.vpk&room=tour-m8w3q2vk7p&live=1"}
  • Body ≤ 2 KB: scene — a published scene path (ingest/<id>.vpk|.vsp|.classic.glb|.fidelity.glb; a bare <id>.vpk is normalised to ingest/), optional room (1–64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; omitted → a fresh tour-<10 random> nobody guesses).
  • Reply: code (7 chars, no 0/o/1/l/i), the absolute url (/t/<code> on the request's origin — X-Forwarded-Proto/Host are honoured), room, scene, expiresAt (ms; VERSE_TOUR_INVITE_TTL_H, default 24 h) and the landing path. Cache-Control: no-store.
  • Errors: 400 not an ingest scene / bad room / torn body; 429 over VERSE_TOUR_INVITES_PER_HOUR (default 60) per address per hour (loopback exempt in development).
  • The table holds 5 000 invites; past that the oldest tenth is dropped.

GET /v1/tour/invite/<code>#

{code, room, scene, expiresAt, landing} for a live invite, 404 for an unknown or expired code. no-store.

GET /t/<code>#

The link people open. 302 to /view?vpk=<scene>&room=<room>&live=1 (no-store); an unknown or expired code answers a small 404 HTML page ("This tour link has expired"). live=1 makes the viewer join as a guest: the Enter gate on phones, then the optional name chip, then following the host. ?room=<room>&host=1 hosts a room at once; a plain ?room= is the 2.7 viewer with the tour bar.

POST /v1/room/<room>/leave#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/room/docs-room/leave -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"id":"docs-viewer-1"}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

A page that closes says so (the viewer sends it with sendBeacon on pagehide), and the peer is dropped from the roster and rebroadcast at once instead of lingering for the 10 s TTL — the guests' "the agent left" chip must not wait on a sweep. Body ≤ 256 B, {id} (4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-]); 400 bad id. Optional: a client that never sends it (the embed's own room join, older viewers) is swept after 10 s as before.

Live-tour signals and flags#

  • flags.host on the pose record marks the tour's host (the host also carries presenter: guests follow the presenter mechanics).
  • kind: "ping", to: "*", data: {pos: [x, y, z], name} — "look here": every screen draws a pulsing ring at that world point for a few seconds.
  • kind: "end", to: "*", data: {by} — the host ended the tour; guests release their cameras.
  • kind: "handover" (addressed) makes the recipient the host as well as the presenter.
  • Guests count in analytics as one act: "livetour" row per session (liveTours / live_tour_sessions in the scene report).

Signing#

GET /v1/pubkey#

The deployment's Ed25519 public key. No auth; Cache-Control: public, max-age=300.

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/pubkey
# {"alg":"Ed25519","spki":"MCowBQYDK2VwAyEABHN2qIj3nOB4cvTPeA0erREzZQC1G4kpkunME6GA0B8="}

spki is base64 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, importable as-is with crypto.subtle.importKey("spki", der, { name: "Ed25519" }, false, ["verify"]). The viewer fetches it from the host page's origin — the page embedding a scene is the trust anchor — and reports signed: true | false | "unverified". It must be identical across deploys; a changed spki means the key was not persisted and earlier scenes now read signed: false (they still load).

Operations#

Two more operations routes are not a developer surface: GET /v1/status feeds the public status page, and GET /v1/ops/errors is the operator-only error ring.

GET /v1/health/deep#

No auth, rate-limited, cheap by contract (in-memory counters plus a touch/unlink probe on the volume — never a compile). 200 when every check passes, 503 otherwise.

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/health/deep
Code
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "4.0.0",
  "checks": {
    "volumeWritable": true,
    "compilerPresent": true,
    "signingKey": true,
    "disk": { "freeMB": 491739, "totalMB": 948534, "usedPct": 48 },
    "lastIngest": { "t": 1790833829990, "ok": true },
    "ingestLastHour": { "attempts": 18, "done": 16, "failed": 2 },
    "telemetryWritable": true
  }
}

disk.ok turns false below 512 MB free; lastIngest is null before the first upload and carries error on a failure. A server storing scenes in a bucket (VERSE_STORAGE=s3) adds storage: { backend: "s3", bucket, reachable }, and an unreachable bucket fails the check.

GET /v1/ops/ingest-stats#

Account auth required (any valid account); 401 otherwise. The last 24 h from the persisted ring of the last 200 ingest outcomes (ingest/.ingest-log.jsonl), plus the client-side failure beacons:

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/ops/ingest-stats -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
Code
{
  "last24h": { "attempts": 68, "done": 61, "failed": 7, "byReason": { "failed": 7, "evicted": 46 }, "p50s": 5, "p95s": 19 },
  "recent": [ { "t": 1790831611415, "idHash": "ace65061d8ab", "sizeMB": 77.32, "outcome": "done", "seconds": 613 } ],
  "telemetry24h": { "canaryFails": 0, "uploadFails": 1, "loadErrors": 0, "lastCanaryFail": null,
                    "lastUploadFail": { "t": 1790832030821, "detail": "HTTP 400: …", "phase": "upload" } }
}

Rows also carry attempts, healed, repaired (verification repairs), fallback and the taxonomy code when they apply. Outcomes: done · safe-mode-used (landed only on a lighter rung of the self-healing ladder — the early warning before hard OOMs) · classic-fallback (delivered through the lossless fallback) · timeout · oom · failed (application error: bad input, ENOSPC…) · storage-full (507 at preflight) · evicted (disk-budget reclaim; not an attempt). Scene ids are hashed. Guide: Monitor production.

GET /v1/ops/leads#

The contacts uploaders attached (name, phone, email, job, whether the email went out), newest first, max 500. This is personal data, so it is gated harder than ingest-stats: Authorization: Bearer <VERSE_ADMIN_TOKEN>, or an account whose id is listed in VERSE_OPS_ACCOUNTS (comma-separated). 401 without auth, 403 for any other account.

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/ops/leads -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERSE_ADMIN_TOKEN"
# {"count":1,"emailConfigured":true,"slackConfigured":true,
#  "leads":[{"job":"villa-3b0cc31202bd","name":"Asha Rao","email":"asha@example.com","phone":"+919876543210",
#            "consent":true,"at":1790873084372,"emailed":true,"emailKind":"live","status":"done","url":"https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/villa-3b0cc31202bd.vpk"}]}

GET /v1/status#

Public, rate-limited with the health bucket: the JSON behind the status page — health, the self-canary's last 24 h and a client-error count. No customer data.

GET /v1/ops/errors#

Account auth (any valid account), as /v1/ops/ingest-stats: the operator dashboard's grouped errors { groups, status } — client beacons, failed ingests, server crashes. Samples can name scenes, hence the auth.

GET /v1/config#

Public client knobs, read once per page by the viewer: { "cdnBase": "", "interior": "ingest/<id>.vpk" | null, "version": "4.0.0" } — cdnBase is the CDN origin the client should range public scenes against, or empty for "everything on this origin"; interior is the deployment's public show flat when it has one (the guided tour uses it to teach Walk and the floor plan); version is the release this server runs (also in /v1/health/deep).

Floor plan to 3D home#

Turn a brochure floor plan into a furnished, walkable scene. Guide: Floor plan to 3D home. Both POSTs go through the same gates as POST /v1/ingest: the per-account/per-IP rate bucket, the key pre-check before the body, and the key and daily quota after it. A build counts as an upload of the generated GLB.

Privacy: the image goes to the Anthropic API only when the server has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set. Without it, only the built-in plan reader runs, and nothing leaves the server.

GET /v1/plan2home/status#

200 { "enabled": true, "ai": false, "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "styles": [{ "id": "modern-indian", "label": "Modern Indian", "blurb": "…" }, …], "defaultStyle": "modern-indian", "maxImageBytes": 25165824 }. ai is true when the AI reader is on.

POST /v1/plan2home/analyze#

  • Body: the raw image (PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF), at most 24 MB. For a PDF, the first JPEG page image is read.
  • X-Verse-Hints (optional): JSON, plain or URI-encoded. All fields are optional:
    • areaSqft or areaSqm, with areaKind set to carpet (the default), builtup or super;
    • widthM, the outside width in metres (beats the area);
    • bhk, style, city and name.
  • 200: { plan, stats, svg, ai: { used, model?, error?, tries? }, repair, validation, frame, timings }.
    • plan is the plan document. It is in metres, with x to the right and y down, and holds walls, openings and rooms (id, name, type, rects, area, center). Each opening has kind, at, width, dir, rooms, entrance and added:
      • kind is door, window or open. An open gap is an archway or a kitchen open to the living room: no leaf, and you walk through it.
      • added: true marks a door the reader put in because the drawing didn't show one.
    • repair is { added, entrance, unreachable }:
      • added is how many doors were added;
      • entrance is "moved" or "added" when the entrance was put right, else null;
      • unreachable lists the rooms that no legal door can reach (never through a bathroom, never in an outside wall). Normally it is empty.
    • validation is { ok, problems: [{ code, message, rooms? }] }: what still looks off after the readers and the repair. code is unreachable, overlapping_openings, overlapping_rooms, tiny_room (under 1.5 m² and not a toilet, store, utility or pooja), area_mismatch (the rooms' total more than 15 % off the printed total or the areaSqft / areaSqm hint; 25 % against a built-up or super area) or room_area_mismatch (a room more than 25 % off its printed area or dimensions). Check rooms lists them; the build does not refuse them (only unreachable rooms do).
    • ai.tries (only when the plan was read more than once) lists each reading: { model, problems? | error? }. A reading that fails validation is read again by a stronger model (see VERSE_PLAN_ESCALATE), and the reading with the fewest problems wins.
    • frame is { imageW, imageH, pxPerM, origin, deskew? }: image pixel = (plan metres + origin) × pxPerM, before the deskew rotation (radians, about the image centre) is undone. Use it to draw the plan over the upload.
    • stats gives the rooms by type, the carpet area and the BHK.
    • svg is the plan drawn for display.
    • ai.error is set when the AI reader was on but failed. In that case the built-in reader's plan is returned.
  • Errors:
    • 413: over the size limit.
    • 415: not a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF.
    • 422: no plan could be read, or the image is not a floor plan (a photo of a room, a render). The error field says why, in words meant for the user.
    • 503: two plans are already being read; retry after Retry-After.

POST /v1/plan2home/build#

  • Body (JSON, ≤ 1 MB): { "plan": <plan from analyze, edited>, "style": "modern-indian" | "scandinavian" | "luxury" | "minimal", "name": "Sunrise 2BHK" }.
  • What it does: generates the furnished GLB. Before publishing, it walks the home from the entrance on a 10 cm grid.
  • 202: { job, id, statusUrl, experienceUrl, checks, stats }.
    • Follow statusUrl (GET /v1/ingest/<job>) exactly as for an upload.
    • When the job is done, <id>.stage.json holds the spawn at the living-room entrance, with a walk view. ingest/exp-<hex>.verse.json holds one hotspot per room and a guided tour, and it is the scene's default experience when an account owns the scene.
    • experienceUrl opens the scene with the room hotspots.
  • Errors:
    • 400: the plan is malformed.
    • 422 { "code": "unreachable_rooms", "unreachable": [{ "id", "name" }] }: a room cannot be reached from the entrance (usually a missing door). Nothing is published. The plan is built exactly as sent, so the build adds no doors. Add one in the plan (Check rooms: Edit doors), or send the plan that analyze returned, which is already repaired.
    • 503 server_busy: the compile queue is full.

Assistant#

The endpoint behind Ask Verse, the site assistant. Guide: Ask Verse. It has no server-side side effects and no access to accounts, tokens, scenes or files: it returns text plus UI actions from a fixed whitelist, which the page validates again and runs itself.

POST /v1/assist#

  • Body (JSON, ≤ 48 KB): { "messages": [{ "role": "user" | "assistant", "content": "…" }], "context": { "surface": "landing" | "app" | "studio" | "docs", "path": "/app", "sceneLoaded": true } }. The first and last message must be from the user. At most 20 messages, 1,000 characters in the newest one.
  • Response: 200 text/event-stream. Each data: line is one JSON event:
Code
data: {"type":"text","delta":"Opening the upload panel."}
data: {"type":"action","action":{"type":"open_upload"}}
data: {"type":"done","mode":"ai"}

text events are appended in order; action events arrive after the text; done carries the mode that answered (ai or basic); an error event means the reply was cut short and no action should run.

  • Actions (the whole list): navigate {path} (only /, /app, /studio, /docs/ and product-page sections), open_upload, load_demo {name}, start_tour {surface, chapter?}, set_view {mode} (walk, orbit, tour, stop_tour, minimap, measure), export_video, open_review, share_link, open_docs {page, section?} (public docs pages only), show_limits {limits}. At most 3 per reply.
  • Errors carry { "error": "…", "message": "…" }, where message is written for the visitor: 400 (malformed or too long), 403 (cross-site request), 429 (per-IP bucket), 503 (daily cap reached, busy, or unavailable).
Code
curl -N -X POST "$VERSE/v1/assist" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"how big can my file be?"}],"context":{"surface":"landing"}}'

GET /v1/assist/status#

{ "mode": "ai" } when the server has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, { "mode": "basic" } otherwise (a deterministic local responder: curated intents plus a search over the public docs headings).

POST /v1/telemetry#

Client telemetry sink. Body ≤ 1 MB, one batch per POST → one line of ingest/.telemetry.jsonl (rotated at ~32 MB, one rotation kept), forwarded as ndjson when VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL is set. Always 204.

Failure-beacon rows — the only record of failures the app never saw — carry a top-level kind:

kindSent byWhenFields
upload-failthe playgroundan upload failed client-side: HTTP error, network error, or the job polled to errordetail (HTTP <status>: <message>), phase (upload = the POST itself failed, incl. edge failures; compile = server-side)
load-errorthe playgrounda share link failed to load in the viewerdetail, phase: "load"
canary-failthe external hourly canaryits end-to-end upload probe faileddetail
lookthe viewer (2.5.0)every 2 s while a scene is live and visible (batched, one POST per ~10 s)pos [x,y,z], yaw (degrees), streaming, stalled, walking, scene, session, vid, t — folded by GET /v1/scenes/<id>/heatmap and /analytics
viewthe vieweronce per scene per pagedev (phone/tablet/desktop), os, app (in-app browser or none), via (direct/share/embed), ref (referring site's class: whatsapp, instagram, facebook, linkedin, twitter, youtube, google, search, email, other, none), scene, session, vid, t
actthe viewerfirst input on the scene; enquiry clicks; hotspot opens and card links; Ask Verse questionsact: interact, enquiry, hotspot, link or question; target (the hotspot id) on hotspot / link
batchthe viewerwraps up to 60 of the rows aboverows: [...]; stored as one line per row

view, look, act and batch rows have their own rate bucket and are rebuilt from a whitelist before they are stored (see Analytics).

Schema: Telemetry.

Compile fleet: /v1/work/*#

Pull API for external compile workers (tools/verse-worker). Every route requires Authorization: Bearer $VERSE_WORKER_TOKEN; while the variable is unset the routes answer 404, a wrong token 401. Jobs unclaimed for 10 s, or claimed but silent for 20 min, fall back to the origin's local compiler, so zero workers is exactly the single-box behaviour.

RouteWhat
GET /v1/work/claimClaim the oldest unclaimed job. 204 = nothing to do; 200 = { "id", "images": bool, "source": "/v1/work/<id>/source" }. X-Verse-Worker: <name> is credited as workedBy.
GET /v1/work/<id>/sourceThe uploaded GLB bytes.
GET /v1/work/<id>/imagesThe KTX2 RGBA sidecar for --images, or 404.
POST /v1/work/<id>/stage{ "stage": "<a-z->" } progress shown live to the uploader; 204. "worker-failed" hands the job back to the origin immediately.
POST /v1/work/<id>/resultThe finished .vpk bytes; stats in X-Verse-Tris / X-Verse-Clusters. 204; 410 = the job already finished elsewhere.

The origin signs delivered files itself; workers never hold the key. Splat jobs are never offered to the fleet.

Fleet bake. A worker that sends X-Verse-Caps: bake on its claims is counted for "Bake for me" splits (seen in the last 15 s) and is offered bake parts before compile jobs; workers without the header never see them. A bake is split into 1 + (such workers), at most 8, parts (VERSE_BAKE_PARTS on the origin forces a count); part 0 runs on the origin. A bake-part claim answers:

Code
{ "id": "villa-9f3a01b2c4d5~bake2", "kind": "bake-part", "quality": "final",
  "part": 2, "parts": 3, "deadlineS": 1041, "source": "/v1/work/villa-9f3a01b2c4d5~bake2/source" }

The worker downloads source (the prepared GLB the origin is baking), runs verse-compile --bake <quality> in.glb --part <part>/<parts> --deadline-s <deadlineS> -o part.vbp, heartbeats POST …/stage ({"stage":"baking"}), and posts the part file to POST …/result (204; 410/404 = the bake already finished without it). The origin drops it into its coordinator's part directory; a part with a different plan fingerprint is ignored, and a part that does not arrive in time is baked on the origin — a slow or vanished worker costs time, never the bake. deadlineS is what is left of the origin's own deadline.

JS SDK#

@ctruhtech/verse-sdk (since 2.6.0; 4.0.0 today) is the typed, dependency-free client for every route on this page — upload (one-shot and resumable, progress, cancel), job polling with stage callbacks, scenes, share tokens, versions and diffs, review comments, heatmap, publishing, presence, operations, and embedViewer() over the embed SDK. ESM + CJS + full typings; Node 18+ and browsers. Full reference with a runnable example per method: docs/sdk.md. Served without a package manager at /sdk/verse-sdk.js (same headers as embed.js):

Code
import { VerseClient } from "https://HOST/sdk/verse-sdk.js"; // or the package, once it is on npm
const verse = new VerseClient({ baseUrl: "https://HOST", token: "<account token>" });
const done = await verse.publish(bytes, { name: "chair", onStage: (s) => console.log(s) });
console.log(verse.shareLink(done));

The route table behind this page, the Postman collection and the SDK is scripts/api-routes.mjs; scripts/api-parity.mjs fails when any of the three drifts from the server's dispatch.

4.0 developer kit: the <verse-viewer> element, React and Vue wrappers, analytics.*, embedCode(), scenes.shares.link(), webhooks.test() and verifyWebhook() — one page of copy-paste examples in developers.md.

The original single-file verse-sdk.js (v0: VerseClient({ endpoint, apiKey }), ingest(), mount()) stays served at /verse-sdk.js for existing pages; new code should use @ctruhtech/verse-sdk.

Embed SDK#

One script, embed.js, mounts the engine in an iframe from the Verse origin — full reference in embed-sdk.md, guide in Embed the viewer. What ships in embeds versus the playground:

Playground ↔ embed parity#

FeaturePlaygroundEmbed SDKNotes
Streamed .vpk / .vsp / GLB / splat loading✔✔same engine, same routes (same-origin only)
Orbit / pinch / wheel camera✔✔shared camera-controls.js
Walk mode + analog move✔✔ walk() / move()no on-screen joystick in embeds; feed move() from your UI
Animations, picking, materials, sun, exposure, DoF, emitters, props, sounds, rooms, tours, experiences✔✔see embed-sdk.md
Voice + presenter mode (2.7)✔ viewers panel✔ joinRoom(id, { voice }), present(), setVoice(), room / peer / speaking eventssame voice.js / presenter.js inside the iframe; the follower veil renders in-frame
Video export✔ chip + __verseExportVideo✔ exportVideo() / cancelExport()embeds hand the bytes to the host page instead of auto-downloading — guide
Review pins✔ Review chip✔ opt-in review: true, setReviewMode() / getComments()same review.js inside the iframe; owner moderation stays playground/studio-only
Private scenes✔ ?share=✔ share optionthe token covers bytes and review calls
HDR display output✔ ?hdr=auto defaultopt-in hdr: "auto" | 1 (default SDR)embeds never shift a host page's colours uninvited
On-demand renderingopt-in ?render=demand (default on battery)✔ defaultembeds park when nothing changes
Upload / ingest UI✔✘use verse-sdk.js from your own page
Stats HUD / inspector / editor / minimap✔✘playground chrome; embeds expose progress events instead

Video export in embeds#

viewer.exportVideo({ duration, fps, height, format, bitrate }) records the scene's tour inside the iframe and resolves { blob, mimeType, name, width, height, frames, cancelled }; export-progress events stream meanwhile; cancelExport() resolves { cancelled: true }. Message protocol for non-SDK hosts: verse:export-video down, verse:event {name:"export-progress"} up, verse:export-video-done with the transferred ArrayBuffer (or { id, error }), verse:export-video-cancel. Details and a copy-paste page: Export a flythrough video.

Exporters#

All three speak this API — POST /v1/ingest (resumable above 100 MB where implemented) → poll → hand the user url — and all three honour the error contract (verbatim app errors, one retry on edge failures only, 30-minute budget).

  • Blender — integrations/blender/verse_publish, the Verse Publish extension (Blender 4.2+, stdlib-only): N-panel "Verse" tab, export → upload → live link with progress, cancel, copy/open. Machine-tested end to end (web/test/fix-verify-blender.mjs). Guide: Publish from Blender.
  • Unity — integrations/unity/com.ctruh.verse-publish, a UPM package (Unity 2021.3+, glTFast): Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish Scene window. The protocol layer is UnityEngine-free C#, replayed live by web/test/fix-verify-unity.mjs; verified in Unity 6000.6 on URP (Boat Attack) and HDRP scenes (smoke test). Guide: Publish from Unity.
  • Unreal — integrations/unreal/VersePublish, an editor plugin (UE 5.3+): Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse. HTTP protocol verified by integrations/unreal/protocol-reference.mjs + web/test/fix-verify-unreal.mjs; compiled and clicked through in Unreal Engine 5.8.3 by the editor automation test that ships with it (smoke test). Guide: Publish from Unreal.

The original single-file tools/verselink-* references remain as minimal protocol examples.
